hooks.text: Our closest stellar neighbor is completely invisible to the naked eye.
Why is the nearest star to our Sun totally invisible?
The nearest star to the Sun sits just 4.2 light-years away.

title: The Invisible Nearest Star
description: Discover the hidden nature and extreme reality of Proxima Centauri, our closest stellar neighbor.

beats.text: Our closest stellar neighbor is completely invisible to the naked eye.
beats.visual: Centaurus constellation sky map highlighting Proxima Centauri, 2020

beats.text: Located in the southern constellation Centaurus, Proxima Centauri is a small, low-mass red dwarf star.
beats.visual: Artist concept comparing a red dwarf star to the Sun in size, 2019

beats.text: It has a mass that is only about 10 percent of the Sun's mass.
beats.visual: Red dwarf star interior convection zone diagram, 2018

beats.text: The star's interior is fully convective, meaning it will shine for trillions of years.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of Proxima Centauri, 2016

beats.text: Yet this quiet fuel burning hides a violent flare star erupting with sudden increases in brightness.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a violent stellar flare erupting from a red dwarf, 2021

beats.text: It hosts Proxima Centauri b, an Earth-sized exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone every 11.2 Earth days.
beats.visual: Artist concept of exoplanet Proxima Centauri b by ESO, 2016

beats.text: Intense stellar flares threaten to strip away this nearby planet's atmosphere entirely.
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile, 2019

beats.text: Ferocious stellar activity is why our closest stellar neighbor is completely invisible to the naked eye.
beats.visual: ESO 3.6-meter telescope at La Silla Observatory, 2016

better_than_last: This episode applies a tighter record structure focusing on the hidden contrast between the star's proximity and its fierce flare activity to drive a seamless loop.
